newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in slow trading on Friday with some short-covering seen after losses in the past week, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 23,940 yuan ($2,885) per tonne, rising 200 yuan. It opened at 23,850 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,800 and a high of 23,950 yuan.
April rose 70 to 23,460, May 120 to 23,600, June 120 to 23,780 and August 180 to 23,930 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell sharply to 22,750 tonnes from 52,990.
Copper opened higher and rose steadily for most of the session.

Traders said that most investors stayed on the sidelines when as the world market enjoys the Easter holiday. Some local investors were seen liquidating their short positions, which led to the day's rises.
"Copper rebounded to approach the key 24,000 yuan resistance level again after consolidations in the week," one trader said.
"But trading was dull with most investors unwilling to trade in the Easter holiday," he added.
Traders expected copper to consolidate in dull trading at the current levels next Monday.
